Question: If you are a middle school teacher, where class begins twenty minutes after eight, what would you do if your student habitually arrives at 8:19?
Old_Answer: To Aaron Chao, I have taught in college, high school, middle school, and elementary school, and if I had a student (of any age) who habitually arrived on time, and was seated and ready to take notes/listen to me by the time class started, even if the student arrived just one minute before I started teaching, this would be fine with me. At least the kid was on time! The problem for the student occurs when the student is cutting it too close every single time, and then a hiccup/traffic jam occurs driving to school, walking across campus, and/or weaving through crowded hallways, and the student gets to class after the teacher starts teaching. Then there is a problem, and then I would not appreciate the tardiness. Because you are currently a college student, my advice is that you aim to arrive at least 15 minutes before class starts. Be in your seat and ready to listen to the professor before the professor even starts the class. If you walk through the door just as class is starting, that’s disrespectful to the teacher. When you start working a full-time job, a good mantra is “If you’re on time, you’re late,” meaning if you are entering the building at exactly the minute you are supposed to start working, it’s not good. Try to be in the building and at (or really near) your desk maybe 15 minutes before your shift starts.
